meta.description: Turns an enrichResult or gseaResult from clusterProfiler/enrichplot into a figure that collapses or shows gene-set redundancy, using dotplot, barplot, cnetplot, emapplot, treeplot, ridgeplot, gseaplot2, and upsetplot. Covers why cnetplot/emapplot/treeplot need pairwise_termsim first, why enrichplot ships no barplot for gseaResult, why GeneRatio is not fold enrichment, and why showCategory silently truncates.

scientific_integrity.detail: All 6 citations unchanged and still correctly attributed; no fabricated statistics in any of the 7 re-executed/new inputs -- all numbers (203/77 term counts, NES range, Spearman rho -0.113, S4 dispatch errors) are real computed values from live clusterProfiler/enrichplot/base-R execution.

practice_boundaries.detail: Still pure bioinformatics visualization of researcher-supplied gene-set objects; no patient data, no diagnostic/prescriptive content.

methodological_ground.detail: GeneRatio!=FoldEnrichment, signed-NES, and DAG-redundancy claims all re-verified against real output identical to the pre-fix run. The new zero-terms guidance and the scope-boundary redirect to REVIGO for non-clusterProfiler flat lists (independently confirmed: pairwise_termsim/emapplot genuinely cannot dispatch on a bare data.frame) are both methodologically sound.

code_usability.detail: Both shipped examples still run end-to-end (visualization_ora.R re-run independently: exit 0, 4-page PDF, 26,699 bytes, matching the fixer's own 26,694-byte verification within PDF-metadata noise). All 7 constructed inputs executed real R code with no syntax errors; the two known non-crashing failures (treeplot on compareClusterResult, upsetplot without ggupset) are genuine documented package-level limits, not unrunnable code, consistent with the Category 3 Scene Override.

functional_suitability.note: Both pre-fix imprecisions resolved: Tool Taxonomy now states 'ORA + GSEA, NOT compareClusterResult (crashes - see Version Compatibility)' for treeplot, and the Skill's own worked treeplot example uses cluster.params=list(n=5) instead of the deprecated nCluster=. No remaining correctness gaps found in this re-audit's 7 inputs.

inputs.label: NEW: Flat GO-ID + p-value list from a non-clusterProfiler tool -- forcing pairwise_termsim/emapplot vs. the documented REVIGO redirect
inputs.note: Tests SKILL.md's Decision Tree row for a flat GO-ID+p-value list from a non-clusterProfiler tool (redirect to REVIGO). Verified this is not a stylistic preference but a hard technical requirement: pairwise_termsim(flat_data.frame) and emapplot(flat_data.frame) both throw 'unable to find an inherited method for signature x="data.frame"' -- these S4 generics genuinely cannot dispatch on a bare data.frame, and enrichResult's required slots (result, pvalueCutoff, gene, universe, geneSets, termsim, ...) cannot be reconstructed from a 3-column ID/Description/pvalue table without inventing data the prompt never supplies. The Skill's redirect is the only viable path, not an arbitrary scope restriction.

inputs.note: Directly tests whether the redundancy pass's deletion of usage-guide.md's Tips bullet 9 ('Make the object readable (setReadable) before plotting so gene labels are symbols, not Entrez IDs') actually survives, and whether the claimed destination (SKILL.md's Common Errors row) is not just textually present but functionally correct. Confirmed: an enrichResult built with readable=FALSE stores raw Entrez IDs ('1029','1019','1021'); applying the documented fix setReadable(x, OrgDb, 'ENTREZID') converts them to real gene symbols ('CDKN2A','CDK4','CDK6'); both states rendered to a 2-page PDF (16,284 bytes, /Count 2) showing the visible before/after difference in cnetplot's node labels. key_strengths: Both dispatched P1 findings (undocumented ggupset dependency; treeplot-on-compareClusterResult crash) are fixed and independently re-verified in this re-audit: the ggupset error text now matches the Skill's own Prerequisites/Common Errors documentation verbatim, and the treeplot crash was re-reproduced identically with both the old (nCluster=) and new (cluster.params=) arguments, confirming the fixer's 'genuine version incompatibility, use emapplot instead' response is adequate -- this is a documentation-only fix and there is no SKILL.md-level way to patch a compiled-package bug.

Both P2s (zero-terms guidance; deprecated nCluster in the Skill's own examples) plus a bonus defect the fixer found unprompted (bogus cluster_method= argument, confirmed silently swallowed by R's ... before the fix) are all fixed and verified by execution, including an independent re-run of the shipped visualization_ora.R example (exit 0, 4-page PDF).

The redundancy pass that moved content from usage-guide.md into SKILL.md was independently verified lossless, not merely trusted from the fix log: every one of the 5 deleted usage-guide.md sections was diffed (via git history) against the current SKILL.md, and one specific relocated fact (the setReadable Entrez-ID-vs-symbol fix) was proven not just textually present but functionally correct via live execution (input 7).

Two new inputs beyond the regression set both passed cleanly and probe real gaps the pre-fix audit did not: a scope-boundary case confirming the Skill's REVIGO redirect for non-clusterProfiler flat lists is a technical necessity (pairwise_termsim/emapplot genuinely cannot dispatch on a bare data.frame), not an arbitrary restriction.

recommendations.title: treeplot-on-compareClusterResult crash is a live upstream bug worth periodic re-checking
recommendations.problem: The documented incompatibility (enrichplot 1.26.6/ggtree/ggplot2 4.0.3) may be fixed in a future enrichplot or ggtree release, at which point the Skill's 'do not retry' guidance and emapplot-only recommendation for compareClusterResult would become stale.
recommendations.root_cause: The fix correctly documents a point-in-time incompatibility but has no built-in trigger to revisit it as dependency versions move forward.
recommendations.fix: Add a one-line note to Version Compatibility: 're-test treeplot on a compareClusterResult after any enrichplot/ggtree upgrade; this may be fixed upstream'.
